title: Key Recovery from a Five-Round AES Distinguisher
summary: AES has a known five-round distinguishability result, but whether it can yield key-recovery attacks that outperform existing methods remains open for reduced-round and related AES-based schemes.

formal_statement.body: Five-round AES is known to be distinguishable from a random permutation. Determine whether this distinguisher can be leveraged to construct key-recovery attacks against round-reduced AES or other schemes based on AES-like substitution-permutation network structures that are more efficient than existing attacks.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of AES-like substitution-permutation network ciphers and related AES-based schemes.
parameters: Five rounds: the round count of the known distinguisher
Round-reduced AES and other AES-based schemes: target constructions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the known distinguisher can be leveraged to construct key-recovery attacks against round-reduced AES or other AES-based schemes that are more efficient than existing attacks.

citations.label: New Insights on AES-Like SPN Ciphers

progress.summary: The source reports a known five-round distinguisher for AES and explicitly leaves open whether it can support more efficient key-recovery attacks against round-reduced AES or other AES-based schemes.
citation_labels: Bing Sun et al., New Insights on AES-Like SPN Ciphers
